subject: Audit rights & cross-border transfer playbook — evidence & timeline
messages:
From: Emma Kelly <emma.kelly@medicomhealth.com>
To: irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@medicomhealth.com
Date: 2027-06-30T09:12:00Z
Subject: Initial ask — audit rights, subprocessors, and transfer assurances

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Redwood looks like a good fit for the clinical triage pilot. Before we proceed to legal review, our information security and legal teams have a couple of specific requests to validate GDPR/US-HCP handling for the pilot:

- Confirm whether Redwood can provide audit rights (on-site or virtual) focused on data handling and subprocessor controls.
- Full subprocessor inventory and effective dates for each subprocessor.
- Evidence of cross-border transfer safeguards (ART28/30 style processing records or equivalent).
- A high-level DPIA support note (we don't need your DPIA, just the sections we should reference in ours).

Can you share the above materials and a suggested timeline for delivery? We are targeting a legal/compliance decision by 2027-07-08.

Thanks,
Emma Kelly
Head of IT Risk, Med iCom Health
emma.kelly@medicomhealth.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

[Attachment: initial_risk_questions.xlsx (XLSX)]
From: irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
To: Emma Kelly <emma.kelly@medicomhealth.com>, procurement@medicomhealth.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-06-30T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial ask — audit rights, subprocessors, and transfer assurances

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (Privacy & Legal Ops) and Karthik (Privacy Engineering) so we can assemble everything quickly.

Quick answers up front:
- Audit rights: we support virtual audits and scheduled evidence reviews for customers under our Standard DPA; we can discuss on-site assessments for enterprise Dedicated/Private deployments where practical.
- Subprocessor inventory: we will provide a timestamped inventory export and indicate the contractual onboarding date per subprocessor.
- Transfer safeguards: we can provide our Article 28/30-style processing ledger excerpt plus the standard SCCs and any supplementary transfer measures we apply.
- DPIA support: we will produce a short note describing our data categories, processing activities, and recommended mitigation text you can use in your DPIA.

Proposed timeline:
- Today (2027-06-30): provide subprocessor inventory CSV and SOC2 summary.
- 2027-07-01: deliver processing map excerpt, DPIA support note draft, and suggested contract language for audit rights.

If that works, we'll upload materials to a secure evidence folder and send a DocuSign link for a DPA addendum covering the audit schedule.

Irene Choi
Senior Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
[Attachment: none]
From: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
To: Emma Kelly <emma.kelly@medicomhealth.com>, procurement@medicomhealth.com
Cc: irene.choi@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-07-01T13:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial ask — audit rights, subprocessors, and transfer assurances

Emma — attaching the artifacts we discussed. See short notes below each file. If you need an extracted CSV with onboarding timestamps in a different format, tell me which columns you prefer.

Attachments: 
- subprocessor_inventory_2027-06.csv (CSV): registry of active subprocessors, region, contract start date, data categories processed.
- SOC2_Type2_summary_2026.pdf (PDF): executive summary and control coverage (redacted where needed).
- processing_map_excerpt_2027-06.png (PNG): schematic of cross-border flows for hosted API and Dedicated clusters.

Notes: 
- Audit model: for hosted customers we run scheduled evidence reviews (1x/year or on-boarding) and ad-hoc virtual deep dives with at least 5 days notice. For Dedicated/Private we can accommodate deeper remote assessments, and on-site for enterprise with advance scheduling.
- Transfer measures: SCCs are baseline; we also apply AES-256 encryption at rest, TLS1.3 in transit, and regional routing policies that can be enforced for Dedicated capacity.
- DPIA support: Irene will share suggested language; we recommend referencing our processing map and control objectives.

Uploading files now to the secure evidence folder and sending the DocuSign link for the DPA addendum shortly.

--
Marissa Cole
Manager, Privacy & Legal Operations
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
[Attachment: subprocessor_inventory_2027-06.csv (CSV), SOC2_Type2_summary_2026.pdf (PDF), processing_map_excerpt_2027-06.png (PNG)]
From: Ana Silva <ana.silva@legalpartners.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Emma Kelly <emma.kelly@medicomhealth.com>, procurement@medicomhealth.com
Date: 2027-07-01T14:08:00Z
Subject: Follow-up questions re: evidence package and audit scope

Hi Marissa / Irene — thanks for the quick turnaround and the uploads. A few clarifying questions from legal: 

1) For the subprocessor inventory CSV, can you indicate whether any subprocessors are sub-subprocessors (i.e., further contracted data processors) and provide contract flow-down confirmation?
2) The SOC2 summary looks good; can you confirm whether any control gaps were found in the last cycle and, if so, whether remediation was completed?
3) On audit rights: would Redwood allow us to appoint a third-party auditor under the agreed scope for a single virtual assessment? If yes, what are the timelines and pre-reqs (e.g., NDAs, technical read-only accounts)?

If you can answer inline and update the evidence folder, that'll speed legal review.

Best,
Ana Silva
Data Protection Counsel (external counsel for MediCom)
ana.silva@legalpartners.com

> On Jul 1, 2027, at 13:20, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com wrote:
> 
> > Attachments: subprocessor_inventory_2027-06.csv, SOC2_Type2_summary_2026.pdf, processing_map_excerpt_2027-06.png
From: irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
To: Ana Silva <ana.silva@legalpartners.com>, Emma Kelly <emma.kelly@medicomhealth.com>, procurement@medicomhealth.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-07-01T15:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up questions re: evidence package and audit scope

Hi Ana — answers below and next steps.

1) Sub-subprocessors / flow-down: the CSV includes a column labeled "tier" where we indicate direct processor vs. sub-subprocessor; we also attach a short flow-down confirmation statement per named subprocessor for regulated customers. I will drop an updated CSV with the tier column highlighted to the evidence folder by EOD.

2) SOC2 controls: our most recent Type II report had two minor findings related to change-control logging; both were addressed within the 45-day remediation window and validated by the auditor. The summary PDF includes a footnote referencing the remediation attestations; we can provide the auditor's remediation confirmation letter if you need a direct auditor statement.

3) Third-party auditors: yes — we permit customer-appointed third-party auditors for virtual assessments under a scoped engagement. Requirements:
- Execution of Redwood's auditor NDA and limited-scope assessment agreement (we'll share templates).
- Minimum 10 business days' notice for scheduling evidence access.
- Technical access: read-only logs and evidence bundles; we do not provide persistent direct production accounts.

Next steps: Marissa will upload an updated subprocessor CSV with tier flags and the remediation confirmation letter. I'll send the standard auditor NDA + scope template to the DocuSign envelope and include suggested DPA language for audit scheduling. Expect the updated folder and DocuSign by 17:00 PT.

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk legal through the artifacts.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Senior Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
[Attachment: none]
